pairmech.mechanism: USDJPY: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while JPY strengthens when global risk rises and carry trades unwind, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 1 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

AUDJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 2 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

GBPUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while GBP moves on UK policy and its own politics, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 3 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

EURJPY: A haven leg against a large, slow bloc, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 4 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

EURUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while EUR moves on ECB policy and growth differentials, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 5 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

CADJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 6 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

NZDJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 7 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

AUDCAD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 8 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

NZDUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while NZD moves on soft commodities and global risk appetite, with the thinnest liquidity of the eight, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 9 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

AUDNZD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 10 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

CHFJPY: Both are bid when risk rises, so they largely offset and the pair moves on the difference between two central banks. It sits at rank 11 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

NZDCAD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 12 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

crisis_witnesses.what: Two more witnesses beside the acute detector and MOVE. Panel turbulence is the Mahalanobis distance of the day's return vector from its own history under the trailing covariance: a day is turbulent when moves are big OR unusually combined. Roll illiquidity is the effective-spread proxy from the negative autocovariance of daily price changes, closes only.
crisis_witnesses.what_it_is_not: CONFIRMATION, NEVER PREDICTION. Both are read on the day, lagged one bar, and validated on a forward-only window from each news-dated event to +15 days that never opens before the event. Neither forecasts a crisis, neither is a state, and neither replaces the acute detector or MOVE -- a witness earns its place only by adding coverage or an independent vote.

l2_restart.note: Layer 2 restarted from mode A up (HANDOFF 0l). The gate 1 on disk cut on W2+W3 pooled = 2011-2020, i.e. on every year Layer 2 then called blind, and charged no costs. The honest gate 1 scores every combination at defaults with costs on, banks each trade by the calendar year of its ENTRY bar, and CUTS ON TUNE YEARS ONLY -- grade and trade years are measured at the same time and take no part in the selection. Four streams, none selected on: trend and chop, each routed and always-on. The cut is swept over its whole range; Jack picks from the curve. Nothing from the old Layer 2 is deleted.

gapfill.note: ITEM 1, Jack 25 Nov -- WHAT A STOP ACTUALLY FILLS AT. The engine filled a stop at the stop price whenever the daily bar did not OPEN beyond it, so an overnight gap was handled and an INTRADAY one was not. EURCHF on 15 Jan 2015 is the case: the daily bar opens at 1.2008, above every long stop held, while the hourly bid went 1.20083 open, 1.16777 low at 09:00 UTC, and the next hour opened at 1.03592. A long stop at 1.10 was booked at 1.10. STANDING NOW (l2engine._gap_px, pre-flight guard 41): a stop fills at the first tradable price at or beyond it -- the daily open for an overnight gap, the breaching hour's open on the FILL SIDE (bid for a long exit, ask for a short) for an intraday one, the stop itself only where price was genuinely quoted through it. The hourly-OFF path is byte-identical to the pre-patch engine, SHA e5264776bbacc833 both ways. THE RESOLUTION LIMIT: an hour is not a tick. The de-peg fits inside the 09:00 bar, whose own range covers any stop near the peg -- so a 1.5 ATR stop is NOT seen as gapped and still fills at the stop. snb_long_eurchf therefore gives three fills: the stop, the hourly rule, and the BOUND (the breaching hour's far extreme). The bound is a bound, not a claim. WHAT IT IS WORTH: on A, B and C it changes no verdict -- the largest move to a candidate total is about 2.3 R over six years and the worst single trade gets ~5% worse. On a LONG EURCHF into the de-peg it is worth -1.000 R booked against a -20.100 R bound at a 1.5 ATR stop, and -20.667 -> -99.949 R at a 31 ATR stop where the hourly path CAN prove it. The leverage cap scales none of it: that position is 7.3:1, inside the 1:30 limit, so capped size equals engine size.

quiet.note: ITEM 2, Jack 25 Nov -- THE QUIET-ENTRY TEST, run as a declared hypothesis because the finding behind it was found by LOOKING. Q is the cut: a pair may enter only while its own one-bar-lagged ATR/price is at or below its own EXPANDING Q-th percentile. Q = 1.00 is the rule OFF and takes the identical code path, which is what lets the curve end at the unfiltered candidate. A bar inside the first 250 bars, where the percentile is not yet defined, is BLOCKED -- allowing it would make the rule look free on exactly the sample it cannot police. THE THREE PASS CONDITIONS WERE WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE RUN: (1) the walk-forward version must beat its own control on the paired test; (2) the fixed-Q curve must be a broad plateau, not a spike, because Q was swept and the best of ten tries is a maximum; (3) the effect must appear outside ichimoku. Read QUIET_ENTRY.md for the verdict against all three.

bank.note: ITEM 3, Jack 25 Nov -- THE PER-PAIR BANK AND THE PAIR GROUPS. The unit of account changed: the 12%/yr target is for the BOOK, so every candidate is banked PER PAIR, PER DIRECTION, PER YEAR as the primary output. The leverage cap is applied over the whole 28-pair frame and THEN split, so a group's R is its share of a book that was achievable AS A WHOLE. Years are labelled tune (2005-2009, may choose, never reported), unseen (2010-2015, the only reportable block) and sealed (2016-2020, computed and NOT reported). THE HEADLINE IS NEGATIVE: the edge is NOT pair-specific in any way a tuning-year pick can find. Pooled over all 28 pairs the selection rule makes -50.960 R over the six unseen years; every grouping is WORSE; and the Layer 1 character grouping is worse than its own shuffled labels (null p 0.987, z -2.274). AND YET the hindsight ceiling for a per-pair assignment is +520.643 R over the same years -- the dispersion is real and no tested rule reaches it. ALSO: pair character does not persist. Trendiness measured before 2010 correlates -0.456 with 2010-2015 and only 21.4% of pairs keep their tercile label. Cost per ATR does persist (+0.919, 64.3%). NOTHING IN THE BANK IS A SELECTION: 28 pairs x 2 directions is 56 ways to find a winner by luck inside each candidate.

meanrev.note: ITEM 4, Jack 25 Nov -- A SECOND TYPE OF STRATEGY: DECLARED MEAN REVERSION, 3 variants, NO SEARCH. The rule is code/strat.py:52 from the early project work (z-score against a rolling n-bar mean, long at z <= -entry, short at z >= entry, flat at |z| < 0.1) and its evidence is HANDOFF_3.md section 9: mean OOS Sharpe +0.109 with 69% of pairs positive against momentum at -0.225, best config n=60 entry=2.0. MR60 is that config; MR20 and MR120 are one faster and one slower. `entry` is NOT varied -- that would be the search item 4 forbids. Stop at one further sigma beyond the entry stretch, target the mean, realistic gap fills, hourly ambiguity resolution, leverage cap, R in the same 1.5-ATR unit as every other Layer 2 number. ONE CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF: the early work's CONDITION was the 9-box (HANDOFF_3 section 10), NOT a half-life or a stationarity test -- the repo has a Hurst exponent and neither of the other two, so both are new and built here. AND THE HALF-LIFE IS NOT BINDING: it passes on 96.7% to 99.9% of bars while the Dickey-Fuller test passes on 9.3% (MR120), 18.0% (MR60) and 90.4% (MR20), so "both agree" IS the ADF test alone. RESULTS: 7 of 24 cells positive, NOT ONE reaching |t| = 2, and every cell that does reach |t| >= 2 is negative. The condition does all the work -- MR120 goes from -83.542 R unconditional to +18.507 R conditional on all 28 pairs, worst dip 222.5 -> 23.6. The Layer 1 RANGING gate helps in only 1 of 6 conditional comparisons and is in-sample anyway. "Mean reversion for range-prone pairs" is NOT supported on R per trade (5 of 12) or R per dip (6 of 12). FLAGGED: every positive cell is over the 10% crisis threshold and MR120 takes 73.6% of its R from crisis windows. THE ONE THING THAT IS NOT BORDERLINE: every variant is NEGATIVELY correlated with candidate A, -0.124 to -0.397.

book.note: ITEM 5, Jack 25 Nov -- THE BOOK. The target is the BOOK's, not a strategy's: at least 12% a year inside the prop limits. THE ANSWER: the best book is A ON ITS OWN, and at the firm's maximum legal sizing it makes 1.135% a year. That is 10.9 percentage points short of 12%, a factor of 10.6. NO BOOK AT ANY SIZING EVER PASSES THE +10% EVALUATION over six years of unseen data. THE GAP IS NOT A SIZING PROBLEM AND NOT A COMBINATION PROBLEM -- it is a return problem. EQUAL RISK PER SLEEVE is weight 1/N on each sleeve's daily R series, so the risk budget is constant as sleeves are added and a sleeve must beat the dilution it causes. THE ADDITION ORDER IS THE BRIEF'S OWN and is NOT searched -- a greedy search over orderings would find the best book by construction. The marginal contribution of EVERY sleeve to the A+B book is reported separately. THE DIP IS VERIFIED TWO WAYS and the worse one binds: the true chronological drawdown and DIP95 over 400 shuffled day orders. DIP95 is BELOW the true dip on every sleeve, so nothing is sized off a shuffle. The prop simulator is r2reads.prop_run unchanged; its breach counts are LOWER BOUNDS because the input is daily. 3 of 6 candidate additions improve the A+B book's return per dip -- A_quiet, MR120 and MR60 -- and every one still leaves the book below A alone. A_quiet correlates 0.856 with A so it is not a second sleeve; MR120 and MR60 at +0.002 and -0.022 ARE genuine diversification and still not enough. Payout on the best book: $843/yr against the $549 fee, $294 net. On the six-sleeve book $144, less than the fee.

item6.note: ITEM 6, Jack 25 Nov -- EXITS, THREE SPEEDS, DRAWDOWN CONTROL. Read item 5 first: the best book is a factor of 10.6 short of 12%, so none of this closes the gap and none of it is presented as if it might. TWO APPARATUS CHANGES WERE NEEDED AND BOTH ARE IN. (1) The engine had NO TIME STOP; l2engine.run_bars now takes time_stop_bars, default 0 = off, checked AFTER the three signal exits so a bar on which a signal also fires is attributed to the signal and not to the clock. At 0 the engine is byte-identical to before, SHA e5264776bbacc833. (2) The EXIT-INDICATOR SLOT WAS BLANK -- stage 2 zeroed x_el/x_es, so "each alone" would have been two arms not three. The family has exactly one member, adx_dmi_exit, so no choice is made. SPEEDS: "three speeds" is read as the project's own half / default / double settings, run simultaneously as equal-risk sleeves. FIXED settings, so the window is 2005-2015 by Jack's own rule, with a 2010-2015 column so the window is not a confound. THE RESULT IS NOT ABOUT SPEEDS: 6 of 6 fixed-setting cells lose on 2005-2015 and 4 of 6 lose on 2010-2015; the best is A/default at +5.692 R against +39.874 R for the walk-forward stitch of the same combination. A is substantially the walk-forward SELECTION, not the indicator at any one setting. DRAWDOWN: steady risk, equity pause, kill switch and crisis sizing, each causal, each swept. Best single cell is equity_pause at 25% of dip / 10 days, +16.5% on return per dip -- the maximum over 25 cells on one six-year sample, so an upper bound rather than a setting to adopt, and the curve is not monotone. A kill switch at 50% of the binding dip turns +39.874 R into -13.348 R. Crisis sizing costs money monotonically.

protocol.note: THE NEW DIRECTION, Jack 25 Nov 15:00 -- LAYER 1 IS OUT OF LAYER 2. Nothing here reads a regime, a state or a label. The job is to find working COMPLETE NNFX algorithms under ONE fixed protocol, results/nnfx/PROTOCOL.md, written before anything was scored and not changed without Jack. A CANDIDATE IS A COMPLETE ALGORITHM: C1, C2, volume, baseline, exit indicator, all five slots LIVE, all three exits live, Jack's risk plan fixed, every setting in the ledger before it is scored. THIS IS THE FIRST PROTOCOL IN THE PROJECT THAT TESTS A COMPLETE ALGORITHM -- stage 1 neutralised four of five slots to isolate one, stage 2 neutralised three to isolate the baseline, so both were tests of a PIECE and neither is evidence about a candidate here. FOUR GATES, pass or fail, no weighting. G1 LUCK: block-bootstrap t on daily P&L above the 95th percentile of the batch's OWN random-entry null, corrected for the batch size. G2 ONE EVENT: positive without the best day AND without the best five days, best trade under a quarter of total R. G3 HOLD-OUT: positive in 2005-2010 and 2011-2015 separately AND on both sides of three currency splits (JPY+CHF, AUD+NZD, GBP+CAD) -- eight slices, all eight must be positive, taken from the WHOLE 28-pair capped frame because the leverage cap is portfolio-wide. G4 NUDGE: every numeric setting one COARSE grid step down and up, one at a time, 20 runs, all positive; the steps are deliberately coarser than l2tune's grids, where a 0.05 nudge on the stop would pass by construction. YEARS: 2005-2015 is the evidence and all eleven years are UNSEEN because nothing is tuned. 2016-2020 computed and stored and NOT reported. 2021 onward sealed. ONE INDICATOR WAS ADDED: kijun_baseline (Kijun-sen 26), N1's declared baseline and the only one in the N1-N6 catalogue the library lacked. Unit tested two ways -- an arithmetic reference, and identity with the project's parity-proven ichimoku base line on 5,844 EURUSD bars at max abs diff 0.0.

source3.note: SOURCE 3 -- MACHINE SEARCH WITH A SEARCH NULL. The honest version of a search: the SAME search at the SAME budget on data that cannot contain an edge, 50 times, and the 95th percentile of the best REPLICATED null result is the floor. THE SPLIT shares no pair and no year: discovery 2005-2010 on the 15 pairs with neither JPY nor CHF, replication 2011-2015 on the 13 with JPY or CHF, plus both off-diagonals reported. A candidate that carries has to work on different currencies in a different decade. BUDGET: 200,000 random complete algorithms from a space of 2.53 billion (0.0077% of it), a first-improvement local search from the top 200 capped at a further 200,000, and 200,000 replication evaluations for the rank correlation -- 600,000 evaluations a run, real or null, every one counted into the ledger. THE ZERO-EDGE DATA turns each bar into four ratios against the previous close and block-shuffles whole bars in 20-day blocks within the year, flipping each block's direction with probability one half; a flip inverts every ratio AND swaps high and low, because the mirror of a high is a low. Daily return standard deviation is preserved exactly and lag-1 autocorrelation to three decimals; direction and any trend longer than 20 days are destroyed. TWO DECLARED LIMITATIONS OF THE NULL: there is no hourly bid/ask path for a synthetic series, so the null runs with realistic gap fills and the ambiguity resolver OFF while the real search runs with both ON -- item 1 measured gap fills at under 1 R a year and the shuffle destroys the crisis clustering that makes gaps matter, so this makes the null slightly EASIER to beat, not harder; and the peg guard's median is a 28-pair median in both worlds. SOURCE 3'S G1 IS THE SEARCH NULL ITSELF -- a candidate found by looking at 600,000 of them cannot be judged against a best-of-one random-entry floor, and the random-entry null has no way of knowing how many were looked at. Survivors then face G2, G3 on all data, and G4. (e) THE RANK CORRELATION between discovery and replication across all 200,000, real against null, is reported either way: if it is not above the null it means past performance in this space does not carry, and that is said plainly.

costfault.note: A FAULT THAT TOUCHES EVERY NNFX NUMBER BEFORE 25 NOVEMBER 15:00. results/nnfx/COST_DOUBLE_CHARGE.md, preflight guard 42. l2engine.run risks risk_dollars = 200 by default and every nnfx* caller takes that default, so raw r is (price move x units) / 200 -- proven on 80 stop exits, where / 200 reproduces the booked -0.5 exactly and / 100 gives -1.0. But nnfx1._cost_R divides by l2sweep.RISK, which is 100. EVERY NET FIGURE IN STAGE 1, STAGE 2, STAGE 3 AND ITEMS 1 TO 6 IS CHARGED EXACTLY TWICE THE MEASURED SPREAD, in the PESSIMISTIC direction. CONFIRMED TWO WAYS: from the engine by measurement as above, and by two independently written code paths that should agree on realised net R disagreeing by EXACTLY the cost on every candidate tested, with gross agreeing to the last decimal. With the divisor corrected they agree to 2e-16 on plan 2 and 2e-15 on plan 1. THE GAUNTLET PATH IS NOT AFFECTED: l2sweep.run_combo passes RISK through to the bar loop as risk_dollars, so its engine and its cost divisor are the same number. The mismatch exists only where a caller takes l2engine.run's default and then charges nnfx1._cost_R. MECHANICAL CORRECTION: R + (cost_per_trade / 2) x trades. Candidate A +39.874 -> about +52.040 (+31%); candidate B +23.934 -> about +51.108 (+114%). It corrects the TOTAL exactly but the drawdown path changes too, so dips, R/dip, prop scaling and every t statistic need a RE-RUN, not an adjustment. A AND B ARE IN IT BECAUSE JACK NAMED THEM, AND THEY ARE NOT COMPLETE ALGORITHMS: A and B are C1+baseline members from stages 1-3, so they run with C2, volume and the exit indicator NEUTRALISED, which is the only way their numbers are the numbers stages 1-3 reported. Every table carrying them sets complete = 0. The volatility floor and the peg guard still ride the volume slot even when the indicator is neutral -- they are engine standing rules, not a slot choice. pairfit.note: ITEM 2 -- DOES A STRATEGY'S FIT TO A PAIR CARRY? This is the gate on item 3: if it does not persist, every searched book is selecting on something that is not there. MEASURED TWO WAYS across all 384,334 algorithms on each pair. RHO is the Spearman rank correlation between an algorithm's net R on a pair in the early years and its net R on the SAME pair in the later years. SHARE is the fraction of sleeves ADMITTED on the early years that are positive on the later years -- compared against ITS OWN BASELINE, the same fraction over every sleeve with at least 20 trades, because the question is whether admission adds anything, not whether any filter does. THE REAL ANSWER: pooled rho +0.0038. Admitted sleeves are positive later 48.3% of the time against a 48.9% baseline in rotation R1, and 51.3% against 53.4% in R2 -- AT OR BELOW the baseline in both rotations and at every one of the six share thresholds. Per-pair rho runs from +0.214 (EURCHF) to -0.227 (NZDUSD), roughly symmetric about zero. ONE PIECE OF EVIDENCE THE OTHER WAY: the top-89-per-pair book holds 2,492 sleeves and 2,426 DISTINCT algorithms, so 66 algorithms make more than one pair's top 89 -- against about 18 expected if each pair drew independently from its own admitted pool. Four times chance. The 20 MATCHED null runs are what settle it.

books.note: ITEM 3 -- THE FOUR BOOK FAMILIES, BOTH ROTATIONS, BOTH MODES, FIVE GATES. results/nnfx/BOOKS.md. Every book is built on its admission years and scored on the other years, so no number is computed on data any of its sleeves was admitted on. a_declared: every admitted sleeve from the 6 published, the 10 hand-built, and A and B. b_per_pair: for each pair the top K algorithms on THAT PAIR'S admission years, K swept 1 to 200. c_all_pairs: the top K algorithms across all pairs, each trading only the pairs it was admitted on, K swept 10 to 5,000. TWO MODES. separate = every sleeve its own position at equal risk 1/N. voting = Jack's 4 September rule, N signals on a pair are ONE position with N votes and cost is charged on changes in the NET position only. BOTH COSTS ARE CHARGED ON ONE CONVENTION -- half the round-trip spread on each change in notional at the bar's own price -- so the difference between them is netting and nothing else. On a single sleeve the two agree exactly; the separate figure agrees with nnfxproto.cost_R on the same trades to within 0.2%, the residual being entry-versus-exit pricing, which nets out across trades. VOTING DOMINATES SEPARATE EVERYWHERE, saving 11% to 22% of the cost. THE BOOKS ARE SMALL IN RAW R BY CONSTRUCTION: equal risk 1/N normalises a book to ONE unit of risk, so its R is the AVERAGE sleeve R, not the sum. The meaningful figures are RETURN PER DIP and the percent a year the B5 sizing then buys. BOOK (a), THE 18 DECLARED ALGORITHMS, IS DEAD: negative or zero in every configuration and at every trade floor, best case +0.48% a year. BEST CELL OF ALL 552: b_per_pair K=89 voting, rotation R1, at Jack's 0.25 -- R +1.122 on the scoring window, R/yr +0.224, verified worst dip 0.933, RETURN PER DIP +1.203, sized x5.79 to 3.6% daily / 5.4% trailing for +1.30% A YEAR. It clears B2, B3 and B4. It is 10.70 points short of 12%, a factor of 9.2. B1 IS THE ONLY GATE THAT CARRIES REAL WEIGHT HERE and it is pending the 20 matched null runs -- selecting the best of 21.5 million sleeve evaluations and then testing the selection is exactly the situation B1 exists for.

winners.note: ITEM 4 -- EVERY STRATEGY IN THE BEST BOOK, sorted by contribution. results/nnfx/WINNERS.md. Attribution is EXACT for the separate mode, where the book is 1/N times the sum of its sleeves; in voting mode the netting saving belongs to the pair and not to one member, so the per-member figures are the separate-position contributions. THE BEST BOOK HOLDS 2,426 DISTINCT ALGORITHMS over 2,492 sleeves, so almost every member trades one or two pairs and no single member is more than 1.7% of the book. WHAT THE SEARCH CONVERGED ON: fisher_transform as C1, ttm_squeeze or mass_index as the volume slot, vidya or wma as the baseline, relative_vigor_index as the exit -- the same family as S3_01, Source 3's one passer. That agreement between two independent selections is worth more than any single member's number.
